Confirmed live during `01b`'s QA: Marcus's self-flag alone missed the curated EMEA co-op demo case 4/4 times. **Closed by `S-MARKET-INTEL-01c`:** `runQaWithQualityGate()` in `MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx` rebuilds the retry-once-on-block mechanism as a Layer 2 orchestration (two ordinary `execute.js` calls — Marcus, then Owen), and computes `needs_review` as Marcus's self-flag OR Owen's independent `eval.result==='revise'`, per the locked design doc §5.2 rule. Fixed with one added `zIndex:1000` on the nav wrapper. Live-verified the full repro sequence (fresh load → click Work → click Bench → click Work again → click a dashboard item) end to end, matching exactly what was reported. Pinned `temperature=0` (confirmed `null` before, `0` after via direct query); expanded live re-test (8 trials against the real dev endpoint, up from the original 6) came back 8/8 clean (`no_match: true`, `recommended_agent_id: null`, Marcus never recommended to himself), both regression scenarios (nadia/tax-filing generic no-match, marcus→owen legitimate `quality-gate` match) unaffected. | ✅ Done | S-ARCH-LOOP-CONTINUITY-01-design/S-ARCH-LOOP-CONTINUITY-01 (v6.3.28) + -patch-design/-patch (v6.3.30) |
| LOO-002 | **[Feature]** Michelle's `agent-selection-intent` schema had no legitimate "no good fit" output — `recommended_agent_id`/`recommended_capability_slug` were required non-null strings, forcing a confident-sounding pick even when nobody genuinely fit (a real contributor to `AA-194`'s live Sam Reyes misroute). **Fixed** (`S-ARCH-LOOP-CONTINUITY-01`, v6.3.28): added `no_match`/`missing_skillset` to the schema, both recommendation fields made nullable, bundled with `LOO-001`'s self-referral rule. **Re-verified 2026-07-16** during the `v6.3.30` patch's expanded live re-test: the generic no-match scenario (nadia, tax-filing) correctly populated `missing_skillset` and nulled both recommendation fields on all runs, unaffected by the patch's `temperature` change. | ✅ Done | S-ARCH-LOOP-CONTINUITY-01-design/S-ARCH-LOOP-CONTINUITY-01 (v6.3.28) |
| LOO-004 | **[Architecture]** `execute.js`'s `resolveCapabilityHolder()` (resolves the single holder of `project-manager` for every `request_help` call, and of any `critique_capability_slug` for a consequential-action gate) queried `agent_capability_assignments` with no `is_active` filter, unlike the roster broker's own separate gate — currently latent (zero inactive agents platform-wide, confirmed live) but would silently resolve to a defunct holder the day one is deactivated. **Fixed** (`S-ARCH-LOOP-CONTINUITY-01`, v6.3.28): added a second query mirroring `isActiveAgent()`'s existing idiom; a deactivated holder now throws the identical "no agent currently holds capability" error already thrown for zero rows — no new error shape, no new decision logic. Live-verified `resolveCapabilityHolder('project-manager')` still resolves to `michelle` (genuinely active) on the happy path; the inactive-holder branch itself proven via mocked Node.js test only, deliberately not live-toggled against real production agents with 5-7 concurrent sessions active. | ✅ Done | S-ARCH-LOOP-CONTINUITY-01-design/S-ARCH-LOOP-CONTINUITY-01 (v6.3.28) |

1. **Meridian Electronics digital shelf compliance question** — `qg-review-intent` correctly blocked (`synthesized_as_fact`/`citation_missing`) because `ci-answer-intent` stated specific numbers (62% compliance, 90% target, 9.58% YoY) without sourcing discipline tight enough per-claim. Confirmed by direct re-test on 3 fresh attempts: still blocks every time — this is Owen doing his job correctly, not a bug, though it does mean this specific question currently always ends in a graceful "let me research this further" reply (via Sam's `pipeline-triage` escalation) rather than a usable answer.
2. **Cross-partner "biggest at-risk accounts globally" question** — the hardest test in the set. Root-caused two layered causes, not one: (a) `ci-answer-intent`'s `max_tokens: 1500` was too tight for genuinely broad multi-entity synthesis -- the raw failing payload showed the `answer` field truncated mid-word before ever reaching the trailing required fields (`needs_review`/`review_reason`/`citations`), the same failure shape as `AA-151` but on Marcus's own core answer schema, not just `agent-selection-intent`. **Fixed:** `max_tokens` 1500→3000 (Supabase-only, same precedent as `AA-161`). **Measured:** 1 of 3 post-fix re-test attempts completed cleanly where all pre-fix attempts truncated -- real improvement, not fully resolved. (b) Even with more budget, Marcus tends to assert precise-sounding statistics across multiple partners with looser citation grounding than a single-partner question -- likely connected to RAG's fixed `match_count: 5` retrieval breadth being insufficient for a question that legitimately spans up to 10 partner scenarios at once. **Not fixed tonight** -- this is a retrieval-breadth/prompt-hedging design question (should broad synthesis questions get a larger `match_count`, or should `ci-answer-intent` be instructed to explicitly hedge/generalize rather than assert unsupported specifics when covering many entities), not a narrow bug, and touches the shared `embedAndSearch()`/RAG path every knowledge-backed capability uses -- too broad a change to make unverified this late. Recommended as a follow-up design session.
3. **South Korea hallucination-trap question** — first-pass result (in the original 20-question run) was clean and correct. Adversarial re-testing (3 more attempts) found it does NOT always land clean: `ci-answer-intent` sometimes asserts a specific unsupported claim while explaining the absence (e.g. "Eleanor's catalog review confirms no entry exists for South Korea" without a citation for that claim) and gets correctly blocked by `qg-review-intent` before it can retry. Separately, one re-test attempt's `gate.final_answer` (after a successful retry on the cross-partner question, not this one) showed the regenerated text bled internal meta-commentary ("The candidate answer's claims... cannot be sourced") into what the user would see -- confirmed this is a retry-instruction quality gap in `qg-review-intent`'s own `delegate_to_agent` call, not a rendering bug. **Fixed:** added explicit "RETRY INSTRUCTION QUALITY" guidance to `qg-review-intent`'s `method` -- retry requests must ask for a fresh standalone answer, never invite the agent to reference/critique its own rejected draft; also added "an incorrect confidence_tier label on an otherwise sound answer" as an explicit example of a fixable-via-retry case (previously only "missing citation" was given as an example, which may have made Owen under-use his own retry discretion). **Measured:** 0/9 re-test attempts (across all 3 investigated questions) showed leaked meta-commentary post-fix -- no regression, but most attempts didn't reach a retry at all (blocked outright on the first answer), so this fix's positive effect is not yet strongly confirmed, only that it didn't make anything worse.

**Verdict against harness/loop/agent/data, per John's explicit framework:** harness is sound (17/20 clean completions, zero crashes/hangs/timeouts across the full 20-question run plus 9 re-test attempts). The agent delegation loop and quality-gate blocking behaved exactly as designed on every edge case, including ones this session didn't anticipate -- this is the platform's safety mechanism working, not failing. Root cause: the Result drawer unwrapped each of `supports`/`complicates`/`consider` with `st.x.text || st.x`, which falls through to the **object** whenever `text` is present-but-falsy — and `complicates.text` is typed `["string","null"]` in *both* `hyp-hypothesis-test-intent` and `intelligence-review-format`, with the latter's guardrail explicitly blessing null. **So the page crashed precisely when a theory was clean.** Two corrections to the original report, both verified: the rendered object is Alex Reeves' — Screen Controls Editor — output (`intelligence-review-format`), not Priya Nair's directly, and **`HAR-9` was ruled out** (that was `max_tokens` truncation; this fires on well-formed, schema-valid output). **The deeper finding, and the reason this took a discovery session first: a deliberate "I checked and found nothing" and an accidentally-dropped field arrived as the identical value, so nothing — not the screen, not a reviewing agent, not the validator — could tell them apart.** Decision record: `ARCHITECTURE.md` §19j + `.claude/rules/agent-section-rendering.md`. **The load-bearing decision was John's, and it reversed the session's own proposal:** the screen holds **no content policy** — it renders what the agent returned and authors nothing. A screen-rendered fallback line (`No input at this time`) was designed, signed off, and then overturned on the principle that enforcement belongs at the agent level ("the whole premise of this platform is to remove hardcoding"). Both rejected shapes are kept on record in §19j *with* their reasoning, including that the session's "it's a fault report, not a finding" defence of platform-authored copy was a rationalization. **Shipped (v6.3.135, `ce5d296`):** (1) Priya Nair's always-fill instruction on `hyp-hypothesis-test-intent`; (2) the same carried onto `intelligence-review-format` so the display agent renders her sentence rather than inventing one, plus its contradicting guardrail reworded; (3) `sectionText()` type guard at `MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx` L2106-2108 — usable text or `""`, never an object, and **no placeholder copy of any kind**. `traits.schema` deliberately NOT tightened (`HAR-14` proved the validator ignores declared types, and a hard reject would worsen `AGT-31`). **Live-verified on the dev preview:** picked a real candidate theory, page rendered, no crash, all three sections populated with real cited content; console clean apart from pre-existing `CHI-64` noise. Two QA items documented as indirect, not silently passed: the "I found nothing" sentence never fired (Priya found genuine complications — not forceable on demand), and mobile is structural rather than visual (`MobileBody` renders the *same* `EvidenceColumn`, and the browser pane wouldn't reflow to 375px in this environment). Spawned `CHI-66`, `HAR-14`, `LOG-54`, `AGT-31`, `CHI-68`. | ✅ Done |

| CHI-29 | **Column 2's analysis scroll box gains the same bottom-edge fade+chevron scroll affordance as the mobile Agent Routing feed (`MI-50`), via a new shared `useScrollFadeHint`/`ScrollFadeHint` extraction in `SharedUI.jsx` — three rounds of live-caught regressions before this actually worked correctly, all found and fixed within the same design session, none shipped broken.** Found live 2026-07-18 (John's screenshot walkthrough): Column 2's analysis content had no visual indication it was scrollable when it overflowed. Fix extracted `MI-50`'s existing mobile-only inline mechanism into a shared piece and applied it to both the existing mobile call site (unchanged behavior) and the new Column 2 box, reusing the exact same values (26px fade height, 4px threshold, `dbounce` chevron) — no new visual pattern. **Regression 1, live-caught immediately after `S-CHI-26` (v6.3.59) shipped:** the new hook call in `EvidenceColumn` was placed after the function's own early-return gate (`if (!qaEvidence && !hypFlow)`), a React Rules-of-Hooks violation — the component calls a different number of hooks depending on whether it's in its empty or populated state, crashing ("Minified React error #310") the instant a real answer arrived and the component transitioned between states. Live-reproduced (not theorized) by asking a real question against the deployed dev preview and watching the page crash to blank with the error in console. Fixed by `S-CHI-26b` (v6.3.61, `829160f`) — moved the hook call above the early return, alongside the function's other unconditional hooks; live-reconfirmed no crash across multiple subsequent full conversation runs. **Regression 2, found during that same re-verification:** the fade still never appeared, despite genuine, substantial overflow directly confirmed via DOM measurement (865px content in a 377px box). Root cause: the shared hook's recheck was purely `deps`-array-driven — this happens to work for the mobile feed (`deps=[ordered.length]` churns constantly as hops arrive, giving it many chances to land on the settled height) but never re-fires for Column 2's single atomic `qaEvidence`/`hypFlow` reference change, with no second chance if layout wasn't fully settled at that one instant (a plausible cause: this app's custom webfonts reflowing prose/table text after first paint). Fixed by `S-CHI-26c` (v6.3.62, `a04fc83`) — made `useScrollFadeHint` self-healing via a `MutationObserver` on the scroll container (catches content insertion) plus a `document.fonts.ready` hook (catches webfont-driven reflow specifically), keeping the hook's public signature/return shape unchanged so neither call site needed edits. **Regression 3, found in the very next re-verification:** the fade now appeared automatically, but rendered in the wrong place — glued to the bottom of the entire Evidence & Interaction card (behind the footer's "Good, thanks"/"Have Priya…" CTA buttons) instead of the scroll body's own visible edge. Root cause, confirmed via direct `getBoundingClientRect()` measurement on the fade element and its ancestor chain: `ScrollFadeHint`'s `position:absolute;bottom:0` resolves against its *nearest positioned ancestor* — the original task had put `position:"relative"` on the outer card, which also contains the footer as a sibling, so the fade glued to the *card's* bottom (coinciding with the footer's bottom), not the scroll body's. A design-spec mistake from this design session's own original task, not a coding-session implementation error. Fixed by `S-CHI-26d` (v6.3.63, `66448ac`) — gave the scroll body + fade their own dedicated `position:"relative"` wrapper (sized identically to how the scroll body was sized directly before, zero added padding/margin), leaving the footer as a sibling of that wrapper instead of sharing its positioned ancestor; `CHI-18`'s locked 14px gap confirmed unaffected. **Design session's own exhaustive independent live verification against the real deployed dev preview after all three patches, not accepted from any coding report alone:** multiple full live Q&A runs (Japan ×2, Vietnam, Crest Wireless, GEO revenue) confirmed zero crashes across every empty→populated transition; confirmed via direct DOM measurement that the fade appears automatically with zero manual scroll interaction the instant a long answer overflows (measured case: 1331px content in a 352px box); confirmed via precise `getBoundingClientRect()` comparison that the fade's bottom edge (522.8125px) exactly matches the scroll body's own bottom edge (522.8125px), not the card/footer's; confirmed the fade correctly disappears once scrolled to the bottom (scrollTop=785 of scrollHeight 1135, clientHeight 350 — exactly at bottom, 0 chevrons remaining); confirmed the mobile Agent Routing feed's own pre-existing fade instance is unaffected by the extraction (appears/disappears identically to before). Zero console errors across every run, including the intentionally-triggered guardrail-block runs (2 separate questions legitimately blocked by Owen's citation-verification gate, a real pre-existing platform behavior unrelated to this session, same class as `AA-143`). Retry behavior byte-identical. **Consumers must branch on `failureClass`, never on `status`** — recorded in `ARCHITECTURE.md` §19j + §1 Harness→Execution. 4 files (John waived the 3-file cap), Node 19/19, regression 7/7, build clean. **Live-verified by the design session:** the shipped classifier run against a body pulled fresh from Supabase this session returns `permanent`/`anthropic-credit-exhausted`; forced upstream 400 on the deployed preview gives `status 502`/`upstreamStatus 400`/`permanent`; CHI renders clean on the dev deploy and the shipped bundle contains the new copy. Live investigation showed the two modes don't merely look alike — they **share a retry path that gives one of them actively harmful advice** (`AA-182`'s "include every field" correction, re-issued into the identical `max_tokens` ceiling). Labelling without fixing the correction leaves the doomed retry; bumping the ceiling alone leaves the next profile unclassifiable. One change, both rows close together. **This row's proposed shape is superseded — as it asked to be.** It suggested comparing logged output-token counts against the profile's `max_tokens`, flagged "likely shape, unconfirmed," with an explicit instruction to re-read `request-receivable.js` before scoping. ## 2026-07-28 — log-99-speed (S-LOG-99, v6.3.194)
| LOG-99 | Speed | **Classification read path: match once per distinct signature. Fixed a LIVE outage — John reported By Pattern showing nothing.** The query had crossed the `anon` role's 3,000 ms `statement_timeout` (measured **3,407 ms** rollup / **3,166 ms** reclassification), so it failed on *every* panel open, not intermittently. Join-filter evaluations **158,564 → 4,074 (38.9×)**; rollup **3,407 → 288.9 ms (11.8×)**, reclassification **3,166 → 295.9 ms (10.7×)**. Cost now scales with distinct signature *shapes*, not log volume (observed live: log grew, distinct signatures stayed 582). **Identity proven: 3,735 rows before and after, 0 differences both directions**; signature assembly byte-identical (programmatic diff); dependent views unedited and byte-identical (the planner turned their correlated `NOT EXISTS` into a Hash Anti Join, which is why they got faster too). Architecture intact: still a plain view (`relkind = v`, never materialized), no pattern name/branch/price in SQL, `pattern_vocabulary` untouched. **Hypothesis tested and DISPROVED — do not retry:** flipping `pattern_criteria_matches` to `PARALLEL SAFE` gave zero gain (3,203 → 3,203 ms); reverted to `PARALLEL UNSAFE`. Node 11/11 on the **anon** key, live-QA PASS: By Pattern renders 7 patterns on 3 consecutive opens, reconciliation exact (3,428 + 19,228 = 22,656), no new console warnings. ## 2026-07-29 — S-DAT-12-design / S-DAT-12 (v6.3.228) — regression retrieval scope, read-only
| DAT-12 | Data | **✅ Done 2026-07-29 (`S-DAT-12`, v6.3.228, `9706ce4`), self-verified QA 8/8 PASS.** `retrieval_scope: "baseline"` ships — a regression run reads the 20 seed rows by their `is_baseline` tag and writes nothing. **Independently re-verified, not accepted from the coding report:** scoped retrieval reaches `fe58cadd…` (Elevate Mobility, `superseded`, unreachable by construction before this); unscoped returns 11 chunks with byte-identical ids and still hides every superseded baseline row; the typo guard denies with `denied-unknown-retrieval-scope` **before any embedding runs** (no `usage` object — the guarded branch provably fired, so not a vacuous pass). Run N+1 competes against run N's own output for 5 retrieval slots. **John's constraint, stated twice: a regression run must never mutate working data — "that will be a fail."** Reset is off the table; `bulk_reset` stays exactly as it is and Demo Reset stays on `MI-08`. **Designed fix (kickoff `v6.3.228`):** `retrieval_scope: "baseline"`, an additive default-absent request parameter threaded `execute.js` → `db-assembly.js` → `ai-enrichment.js` → `search-harness.js` → `librarian.js` → `vector-search.js`, plus one optional param on `match_the_library` reading `is_baseline` instead of `status` when set. Extends the generic `scopeParam`/`scopeValue` pair `SCA-1` established (third consumer, after `p_data_room_tag` and `lib/conversations.js`'s `p_session_id`). Zero rows written, live CHI byte-identical when absent, and concurrent sessions may write to The Library during a run safely — the property a reset could never have. | ✅ Done | S-DAT-12-design / S-DAT-12 (v6.3.228) |

It cannot — `ARCHITECTURE.md` rule 14 (LOCKED) bars content specialists from owning Format Skills, and the format branch overwrites `formatContract`'s schema unconditionally. **But the challenge produced the right answer: re-checking the evidence, all 4 measured failures were Priya's and Nadia Farouk — Data Expert's artifacts — Marcus's `answer` never failed `platform_language_detected` at all, so `channel-intelligence` was scope on assumption. ## 2026-08-01 — S-LAV-9-design/S-LAV-9a–c + S-LAV-9b-patch (v7.0.30–v7.0.33) — LAV UX/UI round 3
| LAV-9 | UI | **`Post-beta`** (LAV is not the §1 beta surface — same caveat as `LAV-4`/`LAV-5`/`LAV-7`/`LAV-8`). **✅ DONE — shipped 2026-08-01 in three one-file sub-sessions plus a same-day patch, all self-verified live on the deployed preview.** John's round-3 LAV UX/UI pass, 9 items, worked one at a time. **a** (v7.0.30, `AgentNetwork.jsx`, `f9bd2b0`) — Answer drawer capped at 280px + scrollbar; every edge that carried real traffic this run now stays solid + arrow-animated simultaneously in its own real meaning color while running (replaces `LAV-5b`'s single-lit-edge spotlight — John's own design, "so the user sees 1 agent's loop requires all N amount of agents talking at once"), labels capped at the most-recent-2 (full opacity) + 3rd (fading); a genuinely-still-open delegation now settles into its real terminal look the instant the run ends instead of sticking in the in-flight blue+arrow look forever. Coding session caught and fixed two real bugs in the design's own spec before shipping: a report-back pulse is keyed the reverse direction from its edge (`sessionEdges` only ever creates `dispatcher>target`), so activity had to fold on a canonical (order-independent) pair key or `REPORT_COLOR` could never render; and the settle effect's own `setVisuallyOpenKeys` updater re-added a just-cleared key on the next render unless gated on `running`. **b** (v7.0.31, `AgentNetwork.jsx`, `5e736b1`) — a delegation target now joins the canvas the instant it's named, not only once it produces its own hop (root cause of "solid/dashed line pointing at a still-queued agent"); deliberately diverges from the separate `AGENTS ENGAGED` meter, which stays scoped to "actually produced a credited event" (John confirmed the two are allowed to disagree — canvas shows "addressed," counter shows "actually spoke"); activity bubble now gated on that agent's own pulsing state, not the whole run being live; canvas arc radius/bench-stack spacing retuned (ARC_RX/RY 235/215→275/245, bench step/span 52/468→58/520 — a tuning pass, not a new control, John's explicit call). Coding session flagged (did not silently fix) a visual side effect: newly-addressed-but-silent agents fell into the `is-done` moss-border state — closed same-day by **S-LAV-9b-patch** (v7.0.33, `9398564`): `deriveNetwork()` now tracks `selfEngaged` (the pre-widened "has a credited hop" meaning) separately from the broadened `engaged` (canvas promotion), so `done` tests the narrower condition again — verified live: a freshly-addressed agent (`upgrade-cycles` run) rendered with no state class instead of the finished look. **c** (v7.0.32, `LiveAgentViewScreen.jsx`, `52d5521`) — the mode badge's 3-second auto-revert-to-Idle after a run completes is removed (only clears when the next question starts); renamed `"Complete"` → **`"Question Answered"`** (John's own wording) and given a continuous pulse matching `orch`'s existing mechanism, verified live held well past the old 3-second window, green `T.moss`, `aiBlink` animation confirmed via computed style; error state confirmed unchanged (red, non-pulsing). All four builds clean, all four Node test suites passing (44 total assertions across the four commits). **Item 9 (an "orchestration mode" showcase visual, John's "jackpot" framing) intentionally not folded in** — filed separately as `LAV-10`, needs its own motion/timing design pass.
